A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PINE research work. Their full text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original RewardBench experiments, retrieval-augmented QA results, and VLM position-bias demonstrations, including Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds molecule-generation, math-reasoning, and further model and baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: PINE retains bidirectional inter-segment attention, causal intra-segment attention, and position reassignment using length-normalized attention scores computed without positional encoding. Renaming segments to documents and similarity to importance, clarifying query/key positions, and applying the method to additional tasks do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds QM9 conditional molecule generation and R-GSM mathematical problem solving with interchangeable premises, substantially extending the original judging and retrieval-QA coverage. Figure 1 also revises the VLM task from naming an object to detecting its presence. The existing RewardBench datasets and galaxy-identification example remain.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained Vanilla, NIA, PCW, and SP comparisons, v2 evaluates permutation and calibration for LM-as-a-judge. Section 4.2 reports permutation accuracies for both tested models and qualitatively reports calibration producing unusable responses. These additions broaden comparisons beyond the original attention-mask alternatives.

E3.justification: New protocols include separate 50,000-example QM9 training subsets for the LM and property predictor, evaluation on 10,000 condition sets using property MAE, and filtering R-GSM from 220 to 95 problems. v2 also adds the Qwen-2.5-72B configuration on RewardBench. Figure 1 changes the VLM prompt and evaluated target to object presence and 'Yes'; existing judging and retrieval-QA settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 revises the Fuyu spatial-sensitivity probe and adds brief qualitative error categorization in Appendix C. The reversed-position and no-reassignment ablations remain, moving from v1 Section 4.4 into v2 Section 4.3. Existing GPT-4V, judging, and retrieval-QA examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Temperature-zero generation was already documented in v1. Table annotations indicate performance differences, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original aggregate RewardBench scores and retrieval-QA results are retained. v2 adds dataset-level RewardBench scores, permutation results, revised VLM findings, and new task/model outcomes: R-GSM gains of 12.6 and 5.3 percentage points, lower molecule-property MAE on five of six criteria, and Qwen-2.5 reasoning accuracy of 91.3 versus 85.5 for vanilla inference. Its new Qwen-2.5 overall PINE score is internally inconsistent: 84.5 in Table 2 versus 74.5 in Table 5.

T1.justification: v1 provides an informal mechanistic invariance argument. v2 adds Lemma 1, Theorem 1, and Appendix B's induction through the Transformer layers, explicitly specifying application to every layer, attention head, and token. This substantially expands the formal treatment of the retained method.

C1.justification: The central training-free position-invariance claim remains. v2 extends the highlighted efficacy claims to molecule generation and math reasoning, explicitly emphasizes applicability across positional-encoding types, and adds the abstract's comparison with GPT-4o-2024-08-06.

C2.justification: v2 explains Chat-Hard and Safety declines through instruction-following failures, parsing failures, and excessive emphasis on helpfulness; v1 instead discusses how position bias can help models performing below chance. v2 also removes the practical numerical-tie caveat qualifying exact invariance. These changes materially revise both failure interpretation and qualification of the central guarantee.

D1.justification: v2 adds the molecular LM configuration—eight layers, eight heads, and 768 hidden dimensions—the EGNN evaluation workflow, R-GSM filtering details, and its prompt source. Existing code access, software, hardware, and original-task prompts remain. The earlier optional deterministic tie-breaking guidance is omitted, without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the position-encoding and attention-mask survey and refocuses the discussion on mechanistic debiasing versus permutation, search, and assumption-dependent calibration. References add calibration, latent-space debiasing, survey-response bias, molecular modeling, QM9, EGNN, and Qwen2 work, while several architecture and positional-encoding references disappear.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and method explanation, with widespread terminology changes. It reorganizes experimental discussion, folds the ablations into retrieval-QA results, and introduces proof and detailed-results appendices while moving the existing implementation details and examples.

P2.justification: v2 condenses and restructures main Tables 2–3, retaining their detailed counterparts in Appendix C as Tables 5–6. It adds nine dataset-level tables, a molecule-results table, and a math-results chart. Figure 1's VLM panel is revised, and the PINE and PCW diagrams exchange order and receive updated labels.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence beyond v1's judging/QA focus, broadens direct debiasing comparisons, makes the invariance argument more explicit, and exposes more detailed failures. These benefits yield a limited net improvement. Removal of the numerical-tie qualification and the contradictory new Qwen-2.5 average weaken the treatment of exact invariance and reporting accuracy.
